newsitem.title: USA: Indianapolis considering convention center funding.
newsitem.headline: Indianapolis considering convention center funding.

text.p: The Indianapolis city council on Tuesday night held a public hearing into three proposed tax increases to partly fund $40 million of bonds to expand the city's convention center, a spokeswoman for Mayor Stephen Goldsmith said.

The Indiana legislature has approved a bill allowing increases in the hotel/motel tax, rental car tax and broadening the scope of an existing ticket tax in part to back bonds for the project, Gail Brown said.

Goldsmith presented the plans to the city council on Monday night for a two percent tax increase on rental cars obtained at the airport and a one percent hike in the city hotel/motel tax for the convention center, Brown said.
Those two increases would generate about $4 million annually for the convention center expansion, Brown said.

Broadening the application of the ticket tax would raise another $500,000, but that revenue could be used for the convention center, the RCA Dome or a new arena for the Indiana Pacers basketball team, Brown added.

The ticket tax currently applies only to sports, Brown said. The legislation would expand it to include other events at city-owned venues, but would still exempt not-for-profit religious or educational events, she said.
Indiana Gov. Frank O'Bannon has received the legislation and has until Friday to act on it or it automatically becomes law, deputy press secretary Steve Campbell said.
O'Bannon's first priorities are school funding, road projects, tax relief and increasing the number of police officers throughout the state before considering other projects, Campbell said.
Brown said the city council is scheduled to vote on the proposed increases on May 19.
